mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 2% annualized over the previous month signals inflationary pressure, leading to tighter monetary policy expectations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns remain positive in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between CPI increases and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 5% signals a tightening labor market, which historically leads to wage inflation and increased production costs, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns remain positive in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between UNRATE drops and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real estate activity (HOUST) signals strengthening consumer demand, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in > 40% of periods following HOUST increases, or the correlation between HOUST increases and positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A significant decline in industrial production (INDPRO) signals a weakening supply side of the economy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns remain positive in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between INDPRO declines and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) grow faster than GDP (GDPC1), it signals robust consumer demand outpacing economic output, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the correlation between RSAFS outpacing GDPC1 and positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) coupled with a decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strengthening labor market, which boosts consumer confidence and spending, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the correlation between labor market strength and positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) below 1% signals an accommodative monetary policy, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the correlation between low FEDFUNDS and positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in housing starts (HOUST) coupled with an increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a weakening demand environment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between weakening demand and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).
